The [[Maldives]] competed at the [[2016 Summer Olympics]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil, from 5 to 21 August 2016. This was the nation's eighth consecutive appearance at the Summer Olympics. The delegation included two track and field athletes: Hassan Saaid and [[Afa Ismail]], as well as swimmers Ibrahim Nishwan and [[Aminath Shajan]]. Both Shajan and Ismail were returning competitors from the [[London 2012|2012 London Olympics]], with the former leading the Maldivian squad as the flag bearer in the opening ceremony. The Maldives, however, has yet to win its first ever Olympic medal.

== Background ==
The Maldives participated in eight [[Summer Olympic Games|Summer Olympics]] between its debut in the [[1988 Summer Olympics]] in [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]], and the 2016 Summer Olympics in [[Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]]. The highest number of Maldivians participating at any single Summer Games was seven at the [[1988 Summer Olympics|1988 Games]] in Seoul, South Korea and the [[1992 Summer Olympics|1992 Games]] in [[Barcelona]], [[Spain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/MDV/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417093120/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/MDV/|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Olympic History of Maldives|website=Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|access-date=8 January 2017}}</ref> No Maldivian has ever won a medal at the Olympics. All of Maldivian participants competed at the Games through universality slots from the [[International Association of Athletics Federations]] and [[FINA]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fina.org/sites/default/files/2015_02_rio2016_qualification_system_sw_en.pdf|title=Qualification System – Games of the XXXI Olympics – Rio 2016|publisher=FINA|access-date=4 February 2017}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.iaaf.org/download/downloadresultinfo?filename=24b872d6-aa05-47dd-8684-790f0edc05ae.pdf|title=Qualification System and Entry Standards|publisher=[[International Association of Athletics Federations]]|access-date=4 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023201744/https://www.iaaf.org/download/downloadresultinfo?filename=24b872d6-aa05-47dd-8684-790f0edc05ae.pdf|archive-date=23 October 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Shajan was chosen to be The Maldives's flag bearer during the [[2016 Summer Olympics Parade of Nations|parade of nations]] of the opening ceremony while Ismail bore the flag during the closing ceremony.<ref name="flag-bearer2">{{cite web|url=http://www.ocasia.org/News/IndexNewsRM.aspx?WKegervtea1dp0XHxrPJEA==|title=Swimmer Shajan to carry Maldives flag at Rio opening ceremony|date=27 July 2016|publisher=[[Olympic Council of Asia]]|access-date=28 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160729133143/http://www.ocasia.org/News/IndexNewsRM.aspx?WKegervtea1dp0XHxrPJEA==|archive-date=29 July 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://stillmed.olympic.org/media/Document%20Library/OlympicOrg/News/2016/08/2016-08-21-Rio-2016-Closing-Ceremony-Flag-Bearers.pdf|title=Rio 2016 Closing Ceremony - Flag Bearers|date=21 August 2016|website=olympic.org|publisher=IOC|access-date=24 January 2017}}</ref>

==Athletics==
{{main article|Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics|Athletics at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Qualification}}
The Maldives received universality slots from [[IAAF]] to send two athletes (one male and one female) to the Olympics.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite web|title=iaaf.org – Top Lists|url=http://www.iaaf.org/statistics/toplists/index.html|publisher=IAAF|access-date=18 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=IAAF Games of the XXX Olympiad – Rio 2016 Entry Standards|url=http://www.insidethegames.biz/media/file/559/IAAF%20Rio%202016%20standards.pdf|publisher=[[IAAF]]|access-date=18 April 2015}}</ref> The [[Sprint (running)|sprinters]] Afa Ismail and Hassan Saaid participated in the Games, with the former in the women's 200 metres and the latter in the men's 100 metres. This marked Saaid's debut in the Olympics, even though he has represented his country at the [[2010 Commonwealth Games|2010]] and [[2014 Commonwealth Games]], as well as the [[2010 Asian Games|2010]] and [[2014 Asian Games]]. The Games were Ismail's second time in the Olympics because of her participation in the [[2012 Summer Olympics|2012 London Olympics]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.olympic.org/london-2012/athletics/100m-women|title=London 2012 100m women - Olympic Athletics|date=9 August 2016|newspaper=International Olympic Committee|language=en|access-date=24 January 2017}}</ref> Ismail finished 8th in her heat with a time of 24.96 seconds, attaining a national record but failing to qualify for the semifinals.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.rio2016.com/en/athletics-womens-200m-round-1-heat-1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826163416/https://www.rio2016.com/en/athletics-womens-200m-round-1-heat-1 |archive-date=26 August 2016 |title=Women's 200m Schedule & Results – Olympic Athletics |date=26 August 2016 |access-date=24 January 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/A/T/ATW002901_Results_2016_08_15_0eb09591_3da4_41d8_9515_f6de19dcaf28.pdf |title=Women's 200m – Heat 1 Results |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920140151/https://smsprio2016-a.akamaihd.net/_odf-documents/A/T/ATW002901_Results_2016_08_15_0eb09591_3da4_41d8_9515_f6de19dcaf28.pdf |archive-date=20 September 2016 |url-status=dead |access-date=4 February 2017 }}</ref> Saaid achieved a time of 10.43 seconds in his heat, ranking first place and advancing to the quarterfinals. However, Saaid failed to qualify for the semifinals due to coming eighth with a time of 10.47 seconds in the quarterfinals. He could not beat his national record of 10.33 seconds.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/rio-2016/results/sports/athletics/mens-100m|title=Results - Mens 100m - Athletics - Rio 2016 - Olympics|website=BBC Sport|access-date=24 January 2017}}</ref>

==Swimming==
{{main article|Swimming at the 2016 Summer Olympics}}
The Maldives received a universality invitation from [[FINA]] to send two swimmers (one male and one female) to the Olympics.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Women's Final Entry List|url=http://www.fina.org/sites/default/files/women_final_2.pdf|publisher=FINA|access-date=20 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Men's Final Entry List|url=http://www.fina.org/sites/default/files/men_final_2.pdf|publisher=FINA|access-date=20 July 2016}}</ref> Competitor Ibrahim Nishwan made his debut while Aminath Shajan made her second appearance, with the first being in the [[Swimming at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Women's 50 metre freestyle|women's 50 metre freestyle]] event of the London Olympics, in which she did not qualify for the semifinals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2012/SWI/womens-50-metres-freestyle.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417165651/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/summer/2012/SWI/womens-50-metres-freestyle.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Swimming at the 2012 London Summer Games: Women's 50 metres Freestyle|website=Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=25 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/london-2012/swimming/50m-freestyle-women|title=London 2012 50M Freestyle Women|website=[[Olympic.org]]|language=en|access-date=26 January 2017}}</ref> Nishwan participated in the [[Swimming at the 2014 Asian Games – Men's 200 metre individual medley|men's 200 metre individual medley]] event of the [[2014 Asian Games]], but was disqualified following an illegal turn.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://zeenews.india.com/sports/2014-asian-games/asian-games-maldives-trailblazers-say-medals-dont-matter_1474993.html|title=Asian Games: Maldives trailblazers say medals don't matter|website=[[Zeenews.com]]|date=24 September 2014|access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref> Shajan has previously won bronze at the women's 800m freestyle event of the [[2016 South Asian Games]] with a time of 10:41.41.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindu.com/sport/other-sports/south-asian-games-three-cheers-for-sandeep-sejwal/article8210311.ece|title=Three cheers for Sandeep Sejwal|last=Vinod|first=A.|website=[[The Hindu|Thehindu.com]]|date=8 February 2016|access-date=26 January 2016}}</ref> The duo did not train in the conditions other athletes did. In an interview, Shajan said they "train in the sea" and that "sometimes jellyfish bite [them]."<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.nst.com.my/news/2016/08/163243/olympics-jellyfish-stings-no-bother-swimmings-plucky-minnows|title=(Olympics) Jellyfish stings no bother for swimming's plucky minnows|date=5 August 2016|newspaper=NST Online|access-date=26 January 2017}}</ref> Nishwan started in the fourth lane. He came third in his heat and ranked 71st total, being 55 positions shy of qualification with a time of 26.72 seconds.<ref name=Ibtime/><ref name="Ibranks" /> Shajan started in the first lane and finished last (excluding [[Federica Pellegrini]] and [[Michelle Coleman]] who did not start) with a time of 1:05.71 minutes.<ref name=Shtime/>
